rows.reason: Operator evaluations are a fixed 3-stage integer pipeline at 1 clk per eval; the count is 16 notes x 6 ops x 64 samples and the cost was measured as a bit-exact sustained throughput, not sampled from a distribution.
Envelope steps are integer table lookups and shift/multiply arithmetic; the budget is a deterministic worst-case clock bound for the longest step path, with no random or spread-dependent term.
Interpolated Freqlut lookups are integer index and table-read operations; the budget is a fixed per-lookup clock bound times 96 lookups per frame.
Pitch-EG steps are additive integer legs; the budget is an upper-bound clock count per step times one step per note per frame.
The LFO is an integer waveform generator; the budget takes the worst case of a fixed per-frame cost range, once per frame.
Pitch-mod application is one integer shift-add chain per note per frame; the clock bound is deterministic.
Amp-mod application is one integer gain modification per operator per frame; the clock bound is deterministic and the path is rendered byte-exact.
Control-tail commits are register-file writes at one write per clock; the count is the structural 96 + 16, fixed by the port structure.
Note-on application is integer parameter derivation plus a voice-steal scan; the budget is a rounded-up deterministic clock total.
Note-off application is a bounded voice scan and integer predicate test; the budget is the worst admissible burst of a full-chord release in one frame.
Controller events store frozen integer scale factors and mark notes dirty; the budget is a deterministic per-note clock bound.
Patch commit is an atomic generation swap plus integer ring bookkeeping; at most one commit occurs per frame, so the bound is deterministic.
Output conversion is integer shift, clip and add, serialized with no assumed overlap; the clock bound is deterministic.
I2S sample loads are one registered load per sample, 64 per frame, fixed by the frame structure.
The SPI write-queue drain is one shadow-image write per clock; the count is a floor-division worst case from fixed clock ratios and frame lengths.
Frame controller overhead is one tick plus a 3-clock pipeline fill, once per frame; it is fixed by the pipeline depth.
